title: Body of Christ
definition: The Body of Christ describes the Church as believers united to Christ and to one another with diverse gifts and mutual care.
summary: The Body of Christ teaches that believers are organically joined to Christ the Head and to one another as members with different functions.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the head who gives life, direction, and unity to His body.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine emphasizes interdependence. No member has every gift, and no member is useless. Christ supplies life and direction as the Head, while His people serve one another through diverse gifts, sufferings, strengths, and callings.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because pride says, 'I do not need you,' while shame says, 'You do not need me.' The body image rebukes both. It teaches that Christian maturity includes receiving help, giving help, honoring weaker members, and functioning together under Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Identify the gifts and limits God has given you without comparison. Receive care without embarrassment and offer service without pride. Look for overlooked members of the body and honor their place in Christ.
